s: Manchikallu and Maidavolu inscriptions belong to
x:
The Manchikallu and Maidavolu inscriptions are among the earliest inscriptions of the Pallavas in the Andhra region. They are particularly important because they provide valuable evidence regarding the early history, genealogy and territorial expansion of the Pallava dynasty. The Maidavolu inscription, issued in Prakrit, belongs to Sivaskandavarman, one of the earliest known Pallava rulers. Along with the Hirahadagalli inscription, it is an important source for reconstructing the political history of the early Pallavas. The Manchikallu inscription also belongs to the early Pallava period and confirms Pallava authority in the Andhra region before their expansion into Tamil Nadu.
Therefore, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Which inscription states that the Pallavas conquered Vijayapuri after defeating the Ikshvakus?
x:
The Manchikallu Inscription of Pallava Simhavarman is an important historical source that records the Pallava conquest of Vijayapuri (Nagarjunakonda) after the decline of the Ikshvaku dynasty. Following the weakening of the Ikshvakus in the 4th century CE, the Pallavas expanded northward from their original territories and occupied Vijayapuri, thereby extending their political influence into the Krishna valley. The Manchikallu inscription is one of the earliest Pallava inscriptions found in Andhra Pradesh and provides valuable information regarding the political transition from the Ikshvakus to the Pallavas. It is therefore regarded as an important epigraphic source for understanding the early expansion of the Pallava kingdom.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (1).

s: Who built the Kailasanatha Temple at Kanchi?
x:
The magnificent Kailasanatha Temple at Kanchipuram was constructed by Narasimhavarman II (Rajasimha) during the 8th century CE. It is the oldest surviving structural temple of the Pallavas and is famous for: • Sandstone architecture • Early Dravidian style • Rich sculptures of Lord Shiva The temple became a model for later Chola temple architecture.
Hence, the correct answer is
Option (3).
